targetPath: /multi-country/argentina_brazil_chile/interests/events-and-festivals/
kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
locale: en
buttonLabel: "Explore holiday tours in Brazil, Argentina, and Chile"
lead: >-
  New Year's Eve on Copacabana and Rio's Carnival Champions Parade can be combined with Iguazú, Buenos Aires, and Santiago. We compare actual itineraries, included events, and additional expenses: the main celebration takes place in Brazil, while the Argentine and Chilean sections extend the journey.
---

## Combining an event in Rio with Argentina and Chile

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The unifying feature is **a scheduled event in Rio de Janeiro**, followed by travel to other countries. Start by choosing the celebration and its dates, then decide how much time to allocate to Iguazú, Buenos Aires, and Santiago.

In Brazil, the event is either **New Year's Eve on Copacabana** or **Carnival parades at the Sambadrome**. In Argentina, the itineraries include sightseeing in Buenos Aires and, on several programs, a tango show with dinner. Chile includes a tour of Santiago, with some journeys offering an optional visit to wineries in the Maipo Valley. Tango shows and tastings are cultural experiences, but they do not automatically become part of Brazil's Carnival.

If visiting all three countries matters more than the event, see the [general Argentina–Brazil–Chile selection](/multi-country/argentina_brazil_chile/). For a trip centered on a festive date, start with the programs described below.

## New Year: Copacabana Beach, Iguazú, tango, and Santiago

There are several options for welcoming 2027. The [New Year Fairy Tale: Brazil, Argentina, and Chile](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-11-days-2027/) lasts 11 days. Its sequence is Rio, the Brazilian and Argentine sides of Iguazú, Buenos Aires, and Santiago. New Year's Eve in Rio is scheduled, followed by city tours and visits to the waterfalls.

The [10-day New Year tour of three countries](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-2027-10-days/) begins on December 30, 2026, and finishes on January 8, 2027. After celebrating New Year on Copacabana, travelers continue to Iguazú, Argentine tango, and Chile's capital. If you specifically want a festive dinner or a hotel party, that is **a separate service**, not an automatic inclusion in every option.

Another [Brazil–Argentina–Chile New Year itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-11-days-2027/) provides an opportunity to compare accommodation categories and the excursion program. Check the date of the celebration, the number of nights in Rio, and how much time remains for the other countries.

Travelers seeking a larger expedition-style itinerary can consider the [19-day New Year journey through five countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/). After Brazil, Argentina, and Chile, it continues through Bolivia's highlands to Cusco and Machu Picchu in Peru. This is a much more intensive journey, with transfers and changes in altitude and climate. The three-country selection includes it as a relevant itinerary, **but does not shorten the actual program to three countries**.

## Carnival 2027: which parade is included?

Rio's main samba-school Carnival parades are scheduled for **February 7–9, 2027**, while the **Champions Parade takes place on February 13**. These are different events with separate tickets. To attend the Champions Parade, choose an itinerary that explicitly includes it.

On the [10-day Champions Parade, Tango and Wine tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-champions-parade-10-days-2027/), a ticket to the Champions Parade and the hotel–Sambadrome–hotel transfer are listed as included. After Rio, travelers visit both sides of Iguazú, Buenos Aires with a tango show, and Santiago. The Maipo wineries are offered separately; the word “wine” in the tour title does not mean that every tasting is included.

The [Five Countries of Latin America with Rio Carnival tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) runs from February 12 to March 1, 2027. Here the parade begins an extensive 18-day itinerary including Atacama, the Uyuni Salt Flat, and Machu Picchu. There is also a [private Carnival tour through five countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/) whose dates and exact event must be compared separately. Check the Rio event calendar and the tour itinerary to establish whether each offer refers to the main competitive parades, the Champions Parade, or other Carnival celebrations.

## Choosing the right duration and itinerary

| Main goal | What to check |
|---|---|
| New Year on the beach | December 31 in Rio, optional celebrations |
| Champions Parade | February 13, ticket and transfer |
| Three countries | 10–11 days, flights and excursions |
| Atacama and Uyuni as well | 18–19 days, altitude and transfers |

On the shorter itineraries, the main challenge is **keeping connections convenient after the festivities**. Travelers usually fly from Rio toward Iguazú; crossing to the Argentine side takes time, after which the route proceeds to Buenos Aires and Santiago. Check the airport used, the day of the border crossing, and whether each city has any free time.

Longer itineraries add Chile's Atacama, Bolivia, and Peru. After coastal Rio and humid Iguazú, travelers reach a dry high-altitude region where temperatures, physical demands, and clothing requirements change. This suits those who want to experience a journey across South America, with the celebration as its starting point.

We help coordinate the sequence of cities, flights, hotels, and attendance at the chosen event. When comparing tours, distinguish tickets already included from optional excursions and dinners. For a broader selection, see [festival and event tours](/interests/events-and-festivals/) and [event-focused trips to Brazil](/interests/events-and-festivals/tours/brazil/).

## Frequently asked questions about three-country holiday tours

### Does Carnival take place simultaneously in Argentina, Brazil, and Chile?

No. The confirmed central event on these itineraries is Rio Carnival. The Argentine section generally focuses on Buenos Aires and tango, while the Chilean section includes Santiago and optional excursions.

### Can the Champions Parade be combined with Iguazú?

Yes. The [10-day Champions Parade tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-champions-parade-10-days-2027/) includes the Brazilian and Argentine sides of the waterfalls after Rio. The parade ticket and transfer are included specifically in this program; terms for other tours must be compared separately.

### Do I have to purchase a New Year's Eve dinner?

Only if you choose that format. Some programs offer a New Year's Eve dinner or hotel party at additional cost. The public celebration on Copacabana and a dinner at a hotel are different ways to spend the evening.

### Why do five-country tours appear in this selection?

The catalog includes active journeys where **Argentina, Brazil, and Chile are main countries on the route**, even when Bolivia and Peru are also visited. The full geography is always shown on the individual tour page.

targetPath: /multi-country/argentina_brazil_chile/interests/food-and-wine/
kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
locale: en
buttonLabel: "Explore food and wine journeys through Argentina, Brazil, and Chile"
lead: >-
  On a journey through Argentina, Brazil, and Chile, wine experiences are distributed unevenly. Mendoza offers a chance to explore Argentine wineries; Chile's central valleys provide a different style of tasting; while Rio and Buenos Aires generally focus more on cities and local culture. We explain where tastings are actually included, when wineries remain an optional activity, and how to choose a journey without unnecessary transfers.
---

## Wine and food across three countries: where the main experiences lie

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} combining Argentina, Brazil, and Chile with a food-and-wine theme. **Having that theme on the overall tour does not mean there is a separate tasting in each country.** Some itineraries include a dedicated day visiting wineries; on others, travelers merely pass through wine-producing valleys or have the option to book an additional excursion.

Three areas offer useful starting points: [Mendoza in Argentina](/argentina/place/mendoza/), the central wine valleys near [Santiago, Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), and Brazilian cities, above all [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), where food interests may focus on local cuisine and urban life rather than winemaking. Specific restaurants, tasting menus, and drinks must not be treated as included unless they appear in the chosen itinerary.

## Argentina: Mendoza as a separate wine-focused section

Argentina's Mendoza lies at the foot of the Andes. Its wine regions are particularly associated with Malbec, and travelers can explore the differences between wineries in Luján de Cuyo and the vineyards of the Uco Valley. This is a destination in its own right: a meaningful wine visit requires time to travel between estates, tour the premises, and enjoy a tasting, rather than a single spare stop between flights.

On the [17-day private grand tour of Chile and Argentina](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/), Mendoza comes after Patagonia. The itinerary includes a hotel in a wine-producing region and a program introducing local estates. Read the relevant days for the exact transport and tasting services. This option suits travelers who want to combine wine valleys with Atacama, Easter Island, glaciers, and Iguazú, although it is considerably busier than a conventional wine holiday.

The [26-day Argentina and Patagonia tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) names both [Cafayate](/argentina/place/cafayate/) and Mendoza. This allows travelers to compare northern wine regions with those of central-western Argentina, but **the inclusion of two towns does not establish that they offer the same set of tastings**. Check the visits and actual terms for each day.

If wine matters more than the number of countries, it makes sense to begin with [Argentina's food and wine itineraries](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/argentina/) and then decide how much time to allocate to neighboring countries.

## Chile: a full wine day or a drive past vineyards

Central Chile has several wine valleys, and we include them in different ways. In the Millahue Valley, the [17-day private grand tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) describes a dedicated day with private tastings; horseback riding among the vineyards and dinners are also mentioned in the offer. The exact wineries, transport format, and inclusion of particular dinners nevertheless require confirmation. These details cannot simply be transferred to other tours because they also pass through Chile.

On the [13-day Best of Brazil, Argentina and Chile tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-brazil-argentina-chile/), the final day combines Santiago with the Maipo Valley. It is a way to end the journey with a wine experience after Iguazú, glaciers, and Atacama, but there is less time for a substantial stand-alone wine route.

On the [Sun, Tango, Wine and Atacama tour](/multi-country/tour/sun-tango-wine-atacama/), the road to Valparaíso passes through Curacaví and the Casablanca Valley, known for its white wines. **Driving through a wine valley does not guarantee a winery visit.** The main activity described for the day is exploring the towns of the Pacific coast. If a tasting is a priority, its availability and the extra time required should be arranged separately.

On the three-country New Year and Carnival itineraries, Maipo winery visits are explicitly offered **as optional activities**. Thus the [11-day New Year tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-11-days-2027/) and the [10-day Champions Parade, Tango and Wine tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-champions-parade-10-days-2027/) should not be sold as packages with a full wine day already included.

Other choices can be compared among [Chile's food and wine tours](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/chile/).

## Brazil: what food experiences add to the journey

On itineraries through these three countries, Brazil usually features Rio de Janeiro and [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The emphasis is on the coastal city, Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain, and the waterfalls. These sights can naturally be combined with local cuisine, but **an excursion program does not become a food tour merely because breakfast or lunch is included**.

When choosing, look for explicitly listed visits to markets, food-focused excursions, cooking classes, or restaurants. If none are listed, visiting a café in your free time is an independent choice. We can help fit food experiences into available hours, but that needs to be arranged separately and is not a promised Brazilian tasting package.

For Brazil, the [food-and-wine themed catalog](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/brazil/) is a useful starting point, provided you distinguish the theme of the whole trip from an activity actually included in Rio.

## Which current trips should you compare?

| Itinerary | Wine focus |
|---|---|
| [17-day private grand tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) | Chile and Mendoza on dedicated days |
| [Best of the three countries](/multi-country/tour/best-of-brazil-argentina-chile/) | Maipo at the end of the trip |
| [Sun, Tango, Wine and Atacama](/multi-country/tour/sun-tango-wine-atacama/) | Casablanca en route to the coast |
| [New Year in three countries](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-11-days-2027/) | Optional Maipo visit |
| [Champions Parade, Tango and Wine](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-champions-parade-10-days-2027/) | Optional Maipo visit |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_chile_argentina_private_grand_tour_17_days,tour_source_luchshee_brazilii_argentiny_i_chili,tour_source_solntse_tango_vino_i_atakama,tour_brazil_argentina_chile_new_year_11_days_2027,tour_brazil_argentina_chile_champions_parade_10_days_2027}}

Comparing tours by the words “wine tour” in their titles can be misleading. Instead, list **the estate or region actually visited, the time allocated, what the price covers, and whether a tasting is a mandatory part of the itinerary**. On longer tours, check where the wine section sits in relation to flights: scheduling a tasting between a flight across half the continent and an evening transfer is rarely convenient.

## Combining wine tastings with Iguazú and Atacama

If both wine and natural landscapes matter, the order of the trip becomes more important than the number of tastings. Traveling between Mendoza and Patagonia requires separate planning, and domestic flights are often used between Chile, Argentina, and Brazil. The Maipo Valley may fit neatly into a day in Santiago, but adding it to the day of an international departure without calculating the time is risky.

For winery visits, arrange reservations, guide language, the contents of the tasting, return transportation, and whether purchased wine can be carried in your luggage. Airlines' rules and customs conditions differ by country, so check bottle allowances against the actual airline and border-crossing sequence rather than relying on a general “South America” allowance.

Trips including Atacama add a climatic contrast: cool evenings in the high-altitude desert, sunny vineyards in the central valleys, and humid walks near Iguazú call for different items in one suitcase. On a multi-day itinerary, this may matter more than adding another winery.

We help coordinate excursion times, transfers, and possible additions. When a wine day becomes the main objective, it makes sense to allocate dedicated time instead of reducing it to a quick stop on the road.

For all journeys through this geography, see the [Argentina, Brazil, and Chile combination](/multi-country/argentina_brazil_chile/). The [multi-country food and wine catalog](/multi-country/interests/food-and-wine/) covers themed options in other countries, while the [Food and Wine section](/interests/food-and-wine/) introduces the broader interest.

## Frequently asked questions about three-country food and wine trips

### Must a food-and-wine tour include tastings in Brazil?

No. Some itineraries focus on food and wine in Argentina or Chile, while the Brazilian section centers on Rio and Iguazú. Check the specific day and included services for any tasting.

### How does a wine day in Mendoza differ from a visit to Maipo?

They are different regions with different routes. Mendoza requires its own Argentine section, while Maipo is often easier to combine with time in Santiago. The number of visits, tasting arrangements, and transport vary by tour.

### Are tastings included in Champions Parade, Tango and Wine?

A visit to the Maipo wineries is available as an optional activity. The exact inclusions and price must be checked against the itinerary; the word “wine” in the title does not mean that a wine day has already been paid for.

### Can Mendoza and Atacama be combined in one journey?

Yes. The [17-day private tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/), for example, includes both regions. Other stages lie between them, so it is a large and varied journey, not a short wine weekend.

### How can I check what is included in the price?

Open the complete tour and examine the tasting day, included services, price, and notes separately. Extra dinners, private tastings, or visits to a particular winery must not be treated as included without confirmation.

kind: multi_country_interest

locale: en
buttonLabel: "Explore nature tours through Argentina, Brazil, and Chile"
lead: >-
  Argentina, Brazil, and Chile allow travelers to encounter humid forests around Iguazú Falls, Patagonia's glaciers, and the dry landscapes of Atacama on one journey. The nature experiences, however, depend on the particular itinerary: some include Perito Moreno and Torres del Paine, while others emphasize cities, wine, and festive events. Compare actual stops, seasonal conditions, and transfer times rather than relying on the countries alone.
---

## Argentina, Brazil, and Chile: choosing a nature itinerary

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The combined geography spans almost opposite conditions in South America: tropical humidity around Iguazú, cool glacial valleys, and the dry air of northern Chile. Moving between these contrasting landscapes is the central appeal of a combined journey.

One of the clearest examples is the [Best of Brazil, Argentina and Chile tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-brazil-argentina-chile/). In 13 days, it connects Rio de Janeiro, both sides of Iguazú, El Calafate, Torres del Paine, and Atacama. Another option is the [17-day grand tour of Chile and Argentina, including Iguazú in Brazil](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/), which also visits Easter Island, wine regions, and follows a different sequence of transfers.

**Simply selecting three countries does not guarantee every natural attraction mentioned here.** Each tour follows its own route. If nature is the main reason for traveling, check for a full day at a glacier, a national park visit, and a stop in Atacama.

| Natural region | What to look for |
|---|---|
| Iguazú | Visits to the Brazilian and Argentine sides |
| Patagonia | Perito Moreno and Torres del Paine |
| Atacama | Valley of the Moon, lagoons, desert scenery |

## Brazil: Iguazú and the Atlantic Forest

Journeys often begin in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), where granite hills, coastline, and urban views stand side by side. The main nature stop on this three-country combination, however, is [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/).

The Brazilian side offers broad views of the cascades and forested gorge. Several itineraries also include crossing to the Argentine side via [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). These are two perspectives on the same waterfall system, not two unrelated waterfalls in different countries.

Iguazú lies within humid subtropical forest, and spray from the cascades adds to the dampness along the viewpoints. Lightweight quick-drying clothing and protection for electronic devices are practical choices. Wildlife sightings are not guaranteed on an ordinary sightseeing excursion, even though the national park's forest supports many species.

For more choices, explore [Brazil's nature tour catalog](/interests/nature/tours/brazil/), which covers more than this three-country selection and allows you to compare different geographical combinations.

## Argentina: Perito Moreno Glacier and the scale of Patagonia

In Argentina, nature-focused experiences may include two very different stops: the Argentine side of Iguazú and [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/), with an excursion to [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/). On the 13-day Best of Brazil, Argentina and Chile itinerary, the glacier comes after Buenos Aires and before traveling into Chile.

Perito Moreno belongs to the Southern Andes' glacier system. Cold ice, lake water, and mountain slopes create an environment entirely different from the hot walks at Iguazú. Even without a long trek, travelers face wind, low temperatures, and the need to allow time to reach the viewpoints. Walking on the ice itself requires a separately confirmed activity; it is not automatically included just because the excursion is described as a glacier visit.

Other tours through the same three countries may omit Patagonia entirely or spend less time there. Check the exact days in the individual [Argentina tour catalog](/argentina/tour/), particularly if the glacier is your principal goal.

## Chile: from Torres del Paine to the Atacama Desert

From El Calafate, some itineraries continue to [Puerto Natales and Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/). The national park is known for mountain ranges, lakes, forests, and open windy steppe. In one day, visitors may see both wooded areas and almost treeless valleys. **A sightseeing day in the park is not the same as a multi-day W or O hiking circuit**; such a trek must be explicitly included in the chosen tour.

Northern Chile offers a contrasting nature experience. Around [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), travelers visit the [Valley of the Moon](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/) and high-altitude lagoons when they form part of the itinerary. Dry salt and rock surfaces, the colors of the mountains, and the night sky define this landscape. The 13-day Best of... tour includes both Chilean extremes: Torres del Paine and Atacama.

Chile extends for thousands of kilometers, so traveling between north and south requires flights. Choosing the country does not automatically mean that extensive time can be spent in both regions without increasing the length of the journey.

## How the season and trip duration change the experience

There is no single “best weather” for Iguazú, the glaciers, and Atacama. The waterfalls lie in a humid climate; in Patagonia, strong winds and sudden weather deterioration affect roads and walks; in Atacama, dry air comes with a noticeable difference between daytime and nighttime temperatures. For particular dates, check the actual excursions available, road conditions, and planned flights.

It helps to divide your luggage into warm clothes for Patagonia, lightweight clothing for Iguazú, and sun protection for northern Chile. Relying on one pair of shoes and one jacket for every region is inconvenient.

The 13-day journey suits travelers looking to combine three contrasting landscapes in a compact itinerary. The 17-day grand tour adds further attractions and a different pace. Compare these options in the [general Argentina, Brazil, and Chile catalog](/multi-country/argentina_brazil_chile/) and the full programs. Prices, accommodation categories, included flights, and service formats must be checked separately for the chosen tour; they cannot be transferred automatically from one program to another.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Argentina, Brazil, and Chile

### Do all tours include Perito Moreno and Atacama?

No. Those attractions are included in particular programs, such as Best of Brazil, Argentina and Chile. The presence of all three countries in a filter does not establish identical stops.

### Can I see both sides of Iguazú on the same journey?

Yes, several current itineraries include that sequence. Border-crossing rules and national park conditions should be checked for the travelers' nationality and dates.

### Is a difficult hike necessary to visit Torres del Paine?

No. The national park can be visited on sightseeing tours. Multi-day hikes and their difficulty must be explicitly listed in the chosen itinerary.

### How many days are needed for the three natural regions?

There is a current 13-day route as well as longer programs. The choice depends on whether you want the main attractions only or additional regions such as Easter Island and wine valleys.

lead: >-
  On journeys featuring Argentina, Brazil, and Chile, opportunities to watch wild animals depend on the particular itinerary. The Sun, Tango, Wine and Atacama tour includes a visit to Laguna Chaxa to see flamingos, while the extensive 32-day itinerary features an island excursion in the Galápagos, Ecuador. Iguazú Falls, Perito Moreno Glacier, and the mountains of Torres del Paine offer different nature experiences. We examine where wildlife watching is planned and which journeys are better chosen for their landscapes.
---

## Where wildlife is observed on journeys through Argentina, Brazil, and Chile

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that feature Argentina, Brazil, and Chile as main destinations and carry a Wildlife and Safari interest. Some itineraries continue to Peru, Bolivia, Uruguay, or other countries. A filter based on these three countries guarantees neither a journey confined to them nor a dedicated wildlife excursion in each.

Landscape-focused alternatives in the Nature category provide a useful comparison. One is the [Best of Brazil, Argentina and Chile itinerary](/multi-country/tour/best-of-brazil-argentina-chile/), linking Rio, Iguazú Falls, Buenos Aires, Perito Moreno Glacier, Torres del Paine, and Atacama. The [12-day tour via Iguazú](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-iguazu-12-days/) has a different structure: its principal nature experience is the waterfalls, with many days devoted to cities. The [17-day grand tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) adds Chilean Patagonia, Atacama, Argentine glaciers, and both sides of Iguazú.

The [general Argentina + Brazil + Chile catalog](/multi-country/argentina_brazil_chile/) allows comparisons without a thematic limit. For scenery, see the [three-country Nature selection](/multi-country/argentina_brazil_chile/interests/nature/); the [multi-country Wildlife and Safari selection](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/) helps identify other routes with wildlife experiences.

## Included observations: flamingos in Atacama and the Galápagos

On the [Sun, Tango, Wine and Atacama tour](/multi-country/tour/sun-tango-wine-atacama/), day 13 includes Miscanti and Miñiques lagoons, followed by the Atacama Salt Flat and Laguna Chaxa for flamingo watching. The following day, the road from the El Tatio geysers passes through high-altitude valleys where vicuñas and vizcachas may be seen. Encounters with particular animals are not guaranteed.

The [32-day journey through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) includes Argentina, Brazil, and Chile, but its principal day for observing birds, sea lions, and iguanas is in Ecuador's Galápagos Islands. One of two island alternatives is included: North Seymour and Bachas, or South Plaza and Cape Carrión. Both options are not promised simultaneously.

## Brazil: humid forest and Iguazú Falls

In Brazil's [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), the main attraction is the enormous waterfall system surrounded by forest. Viewpoint walks reveal broad panoramas of the cascades, while separate excursions may offer a closer look at the river and forest.

The [Best of Brazil, Argentina and Chile tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-brazil-argentina-chile/) mentions Macuco Safari and the Bird Park near Iguazú. **The Bird Park is an organized visit featuring aviaries, not a guarantee of seeing those birds in the wild.** Macuco Safari is a forest and boat excursion toward the waterfalls, which in itself does not constitute a dedicated wildlife-watching program. On other tours, the Bird Park is offered for an additional fee. Its presence in the region does not mean that admission and transport are already included on every itinerary.

Rio is also surrounded by green mountains and Tijuca Forest, but a city tour to Corcovado differs from a guided natural-history walk. If birds and animals are the main interest, check the specific excursion instead of focusing only on the scenery.

## Argentina: the other side of Iguazú and Patagonia's glaciers

The Argentine side of Iguazú complements the Brazilian side: trails and viewpoints reveal different sections of the cascades from new angles. On current itineraries, these two sides typically occupy separate sightseeing days. Forest ecosystems surround the falls, but no timetable can guarantee an encounter with any particular animal.

Longer itineraries add [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) and [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) in Los Glaciares National Park. Here the main nature experience is the ice, lake, and mountain scenery. **An excursion to the glacier is not wildlife watching:** people choose it for the glacial environment and accessible viewpoints.

On the [13-day sightseeing tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-brazil-argentina-chile/), the Argentine glacier visit is followed by travel into Chilean Patagonia. Appropriate clothing, time for the drive, and readiness for changing weather are all important.

## Chile: Torres del Paine, birds, and the Atacama Desert

[Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) combines mountains, steppe, forests, and glacial lakes. On the [Best of Brazil, Argentina and Chile tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-brazil-argentina-chile/), a park excursion includes Lakes Pehoé and Grey. The area's wildlife description mentions guanacos, foxes, pumas, and Andean condors. **These are species found in the area, not a promise that every species will be encountered.** In particular, a standard sightseeing tour should not be mistaken for a specialized puma-tracking excursion.

Another Chilean nature region is [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), with the Valley of the Moon, salt flats, and lagoons. On [Sun, Tango, Wine and Atacama](/multi-country/tour/sun-tango-wine-atacama/), day 13 includes Laguna Chaxa with flamingo observation. This is a substantive difference from a simple visit to desert scenery or the Valley of the Moon: the program explicitly includes watching birds in their natural habitat.

## Scenic alternatives to wildlife watching

| Goal | What to choose |

| Waterfalls and forest | Both sides of Iguazú |

Travelers with limited time may want to focus on Iguazú and the principal cities. Glaciers and Torres del Paine require additional long-distance flights and transfers. Adding Atacama also means accounting for northern Chile's dry climate and altitude. Fitting every nature region into a short itinerary without reducing the time spent at each is difficult.

Each balances nature, cities, and travel time differently.

## Seasons, safety, and preparation

Brazil's Iguazú region, Argentine Patagonia, and northern Chile have different climates. At the waterfalls, humidity and protection from spray matter; in Patagonia, wind and layered clothing; in Atacama, dry air, sunshine, and marked temperature changes between day and night. There is no meaningful single “best weather for all three countries” without specifying the regions and months.

The journey also involves flights, road transfers, and border crossings. We help coordinate the sequence of stops, buffer times between connections, preferred pace, and baggage needs. National park conditions, medical restrictions, entry rules, and payment arrangements require specific checks for the traveler's nationality, dates, and route; no tour can guarantee wild animals appearing at a scheduled hour.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Argentina, Brazil, and Chile

### Can I see Iguazú from both sides on one trip?

Yes. Several current tours visit the Brazilian and Argentine sides on different days. Check the excursions and tickets included on the chosen itinerary.

### Does Torres del Paine guarantee seeing a puma?

No. Pumas live in the region, but an ordinary park sightseeing excursion is not the same as a specialist predator-watching experience and does not guarantee an encounter.

### How is the Iguazú Bird Park different from birdwatching in Atacama?

The Bird Park is an organized site with aviaries. At Atacama's natural lagoons and protected areas, observation takes place in natural habitats and depends on season, access, and bird behavior.

### Are 12 days enough for Iguazú, glaciers, and Atacama?

The [12-day tour via Iguazú](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-iguazu-12-days/) focuses on the waterfalls and cities, without a complete Patagonia glacier section. Choose a longer itinerary for several distant natural regions and compare how many days it allocates to each.

### Do all tours in this selection visit only three countries?

No. It also contains broader itineraries where Argentina, Brazil, and Chile are part of a journey through four or more countries. Each tour page lists its full route.

### Is special preparation needed for Chile's high-altitude section?

Yes. For high-altitude regions, assess exertion, elevations, and personal health before departure. The level of difficulty depends on the particular excursion day; a sightseeing drive and a long hike require different preparation.

## Argentina, Brazil, Chile, and Colombia: the actual itinerary

This selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} passing through all four countries. Our [32-day eight-country South America tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) also visits Uruguay, Bolivia, Peru, and Ecuador. Countries named in a filter are present on the route; the selection does not represent a separate four-country itinerary.

The combination covers several very different regions: Atlantic [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), Iguazú Falls on the Brazil–Argentina border, [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and Atacama, followed by [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), and [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/). Unlike a tour of neighboring capitals, this trip has substantial independent sections between some of the listed countries.

## Brazil and Argentina: waterfalls on both sides of the border

The journey begins with arrival in [São Paulo](/brazil/place/sao-paulo/) and a flight to [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). Excursions to Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain are planned, followed by a flight to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). After seeing the waterfalls from the Brazilian side, travelers visit the [Argentine Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/).

Exploring both sides offers different views of the cascades and requires crossing an international border. Travelers need to consider not only attraction tickets but also the entry and re-entry rules applicable to their passports. The Bird Park and Macuco Safari are optional paid activities; they are not automatically included in the waterfall excursion.

Travelers then continue to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) for sightseeing and tango with dinner. The next day brings a ferry excursion to Montevideo and a return to Argentina. Only after Uruguay does the journey fly to Chile. Those who prefer to focus on the Atlantic side can compare [Brazil and Argentina tours](/multi-country/argentina_brazil/).

## Chile: city and desert at the beginning of the Andean section

After Argentina, the route passes through [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), followed by a flight to Calama and a transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). From Atacama, the group continues by off-road vehicle into Bolivia. The Bolivian section features high-altitude lagoons and the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), then La Paz.

This is a significant feature of our tour: Chile is linked to Bolivia by an overland crossing, not by a direct flight to Colombia. Sections of the highland road exceed 4,000 m, and there is an overnight stay in an expedition-style hotel. Preparation differs from sightseeing in Buenos Aires or Santiago: warm clothing, sun protection, and assessment of altitude tolerance are important.

After Bolivia, the program continues through Peru and Ecuador. Removing these countries and sending travelers straight to Colombia would require recalculating the flights, accommodation, and excursion program. For a shorter geographical combination, see [Argentina, Brazil, and Chile](/multi-country/argentina_brazil_chile/).

## Colombia: a finale featuring three cities

Travelers arrive in Colombia on a flight from Guayaquil, following the Ecuadorian section with the Galápagos Islands. The first stop is [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/): an excursion to Guatapé and El Peñón Rock is planned nearby, and Comuna 13 is also on the program. A flight then takes the group to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) for a sightseeing day, followed by travel to [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/). The capital area itinerary includes Monserrate and the [Salt Cathedral at Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/).

Colombia occupies several days rather than being merely an airport connection. Even here, however, the program has little scope for arbitrary extensions: domestic flights and the final departure are already linked within the wider itinerary. Travelers interested in a deeper exploration of Colombia can compare [stand-alone Colombia tours](/colombia/tour/).

## Weather, luggage, and physical demands

The major climate contrasts are warm, humid Brazil; urban Chile; dry Atacama; the cold nights of Bolivia's highlands; and, later, warmer Cartagena. A suitcase packed for a single “summer” climate would be impractical. Plan layered clothing, closed shoes for mountain outings, sun protection, and light clothes for the coast.

Altitude is especially relevant on the Chile–Bolivia crossing. Even athletic fitness does not guarantee freedom from altitude sickness; the rate of ascent and individual reaction matter. Before departure, check the altitude of overnight stops and any medical contraindications. An ordinary sightseeing day in Santiago does not indicate how someone will cope with the Altiplano.

## Documents and money for four highlighted countries within an eight-country tour

Brazil uses the real; Argentina the Argentine peso; Chile the Chilean peso; and Colombia the Colombian peso. The full itinerary adds other currencies and varying payment conditions. Whether a particular bank card works depends on the issuing bank and local infrastructure. For remote sections, it is useful to arrange a reserve of accessible cash.

Entry rules must be checked for each traveler's nationality and all eight countries, including the crossing at Iguazú and the overland Chile–Bolivia border. Ada Tours helps organize flights and transfers, review documentation, and prepare for contrasting climates. Included services, prices, and health considerations must always be checked against the chosen program.

## How to decide whether the route suits you

Choose the full journey if you are comfortable with frequent transfers in exchange for Rio, Iguazú, Argentina's capital, the desert, and Colombian cities together with attractions in the countries between them. If a gentler pace and several nights in one place are more important, consider [Brazil with Argentina](/multi-country/argentina_brazil/) or [Argentina with Chile](/multi-country/argentina_chile/) separately.

Reducing the eight-country journey changes more than the price: it changes the substance of the trip. Our itinerary does not contain direct connections between the four selected countries as a stand-alone route. A dedicated four-country option requires separate route planning.
